## 9c5eacd4de3e

**Reproduced lesson ambiguity: token values can be ignored.** Generator SHA-256 is `d6daa955369688f0c417b78b782b5cc373cefda047afa68ce8ad95c52abb5fc4`; executed rule hash is `035038dcf117` (rule-text SHA-256 `24f2b28678398850863812e6472a7ae22e0f5a7e5b8189dbe1883bcde0bc1ebd`).

At medium difficulty, seed 97 and sample indices 0–3 form an exact three-demo/one-query counterexample. The rival “ignore token values and sort object crops by their original left edge” matches the Racket output on samples **0, 1, and 2**, but differs on held-out sample **3**. In the query, left-to-right color order is `[8,9]`, while token order is `[9,8]`. All four inputs were produced by the generator and pass its `self_check` (`checks/audit/9c5eacd4de3e/lesson-probe.json`; hashes and comparison results in `checks/audit/9c5eacd4de3e/counterexample.json`; full Racket evidence in `checks/audit/9c5eacd4de3e/racket.json`).

This is a concrete teaching defect for any assembler that selects those three demonstrations and query; it is not a claim that every production lesson is ambiguous. The target has no executable lesson rival contract to reject such a schedule.

**Additional reproduced contract issue.** The source advertises `grid_h=8..14`, but `generate(0,0,difficulty='easy',grid_h=8)` raises `ValueError: draw_int('grid_h'): override 8 outside [9, 10]`. Lint also fails for a missing `RULE_HASH` (`checks/audit/9c5eacd4de3e/lint/checks/9c5eacd4de3e_after_lint.log`).

**Suggested repair, not applied.** Add a left-to-right rival, require at least one demonstration whose token order differs from spatial order, validate exact object/token counts and distinct keys, and make axis domains exact across bands.

## 9c5eacd4de3e

**Reproduced lesson ambiguity: token values can be ignored.** Generator SHA-256 is
`d6daa955369688f0c417b78b782b5cc373cefda047afa68ce8ad95c52abb5fc4`;
executed canonical rule hash is `035038dcf117` (rule-text SHA-256
`24f2b28678398850863812e6472a7ae22e0f5a7e5b8189dbe1883bcde0bc1ebd`).

At medium difficulty, seed `97`, sample indices `0..3` form an exact
three-demonstration/one-query counterexample. The rival “ignore token values and sort
object crops by original left edge” matches Racket outputs for samples 0, 1, and 2,
but differs on held-out sample 3. All four generator inputs pass `self_check` and belong
to the documented ordinary domain. See
`checks/audit/9c5eacd4de3e/counterexample.json`, complete Racket evidence in
`checks/audit/9c5eacd4de3e/racket.json`, and rival outputs in
`checks/audit/9c5eacd4de3e/rival.json`.

This is a concrete teaching defect for any assembler choosing those samples, not a

from spatial order; also validate exact object/token counts and distinct keys. The lint
stage independently fails for a missing `RULE_HASH`; see
`checks/audit/9c5eacd4de3e-lint/checks/9c5eacd4de3e_before_lint.log`. No audit-target
source was changed.
